summary: The candelabra had been sent to E.J.Dwyer P/L for restoration as arranged at the previous meeting.
quote:
(i) The candelabra had been sent to E.J.Dwyer P/L.
for restoration as arranged at the previous
meeting.

summary: The Trustees agreed to give Reverend Bathgate permission to bring invited guests to morning tea at Vaucluse House on the special occasion.
quote:
(ii) He had received an invitation from Reverend
Bathgate of the Wentworth Memorial Church
requesting his presence at a special Morning
Prayer Service to commemorate the centenary
of Wentworth's death. Later Reverend Bathgate
telephoned asking permission to bring the
invited guests to morning tea at Vaucluse
House. After discussion by the Trustees, it
was agreed that permission be given on this
special occasion, the members of the church
committee to act as hosts. The President
intimated that he would be in communication
again with Reverend Bathgate, as he understood
the Trustees were to be present at the function.

summary: It was resolved that, if the occasion arises, the Chairman have a casting vote in addition to his personal vote as a matter of procedure.
quote:
On the motion of Mr.Miller, seconded by Mr.Yelland,
it was resolved that, if the occasion arises, the
Chairman have a casting vote, in addition to his
personal vote as a matter of procedure.

summary: The National Parks Service confirmed that personal accident insurance benefits would apply to Trustees injured while carrying out their duties.
quote:
(i) National Parks Service in reply to Trust's
letter in reference to Personal Accident
Insurance, informing the Trust that, as
previously outlined in their earlier letter,
the benefits available to Trustees would apply
in the event of any Trustee, while carrying out
his duties in that capacity, suffer any injury.

summary: Mr. Miller outlined the Equity Trustees' position regarding Broughton Hay's Estate and the meeting resolved that he draft another letter seeking further information.
red_flag_reason: Further information was still needed from the Equity Trustees about Broughton Hay's Estate.
quote:
(ii) The Equity Trustees re Broughton Hay's Estate
and Trust's reply thereto. Mr.Miller outlined
the position to the Trustees and it was
resolved that Mr.Miller draft another letter to
the Equity Trustees seeking further information.

summary: The meeting accepted R.Contato's quotation of $208.00 for stripping, undercoating and painting seventeen garden seats white.
quote:
(1) Quotation from R.Contato to the amount of
$208-00 for the stripping,undercoating and
painting of seventeen garden seats was
accepted, the seats to be painted white.

asset: corrugated iron roof, timber frames, iron arches and posts
summary: The meeting accepted R.Contato's June 1970 quotation for restoring the corrugated iron roof, timber frames, iron arches and posts at $2,690.00, with $1,300.00 allocated by the National Parks Service and the balance to be paid from the Special Purchase Account.
red_flag_reason: The National Parks Service allocated only $1,300.00 toward the $2,690.00 roof restoration, leaving the balance to be paid from the Special Purchase Account.
quote:
(ii) The restoration of corrugated iron roof,
timber frames, iron arches and posts, was
discussed in the light of the expected visit
of the Governor, Sir Roden Cutler, at the
Wentworth Commemoration ceremony. It was
resolved that the quotation of "Procedure No.2"
as presented by R.Contato in June,1970, be
accepted at a cost of $2,690-00. As the
National Parks Service had allocated $1,300-00
towards this work, the balance would be paid
from the Special Purchase Account.

summary: The Secretary's Report was received and discussed.
quote: The Secretary's Report was received and discussed.

summary: The statement showing the Trust's financial position as at close of business on 31 January 1972 was discussed and noted.
quote:
(i) Statement showing financial position of the
Trust as at close of business on 31/1/72
was discussed and noted.

summary: Accounts paid since the December meeting, including $1,251.89 as shown on Recoupment Summary No.20, were confirmed.
quote:
(ii) On the motion of Mr.Yelland, seconded by
Mr.Barrett, accounts paid since December
meeting to the value of $1251-89, $1271-29,
$2211-02, $2354-86, $2613-70,$2895-90 as
shown on Recoupment Summaries Nos.20,21,22,
23,24 and 25, were confirmed.

summary: The meeting agreed to combine the Trust's later commemoration ceremony with the launching of the Friends of Vaucluse House project, leaving the matter to Messrs. Finlay and Yelland.
quote:
In a report on the progress of the Friends of Vaucluse
House project, Mr.Finlay suggested that the
commemoration ceremony planned by the Trust later
in the year be combined with the launching of the
Friends of Vaucluse House project. This was agreed
to and the matter was left in the hands of Messrs.
Finlay and Yelland.

summary: The Trustees decided to write to the National Parks Service about the delay in agreement with the Maritime Services Board over responsibility for maintaining the Nielsen Park wharf, noting public-safety risk and urging expert advice urgently.
counterparty: National Parks Service and Maritime Services Board
red_flag_reason: Responsibility for maintaining the wharf was unresolved, repairs were lacking, and deterioration could endanger public safety.
quote:
The question of the wharf at Nielsen Park was
discussed and it was decided that a letter be sent
to the National Parks Service expressing concern at
the delay in the Service and the Maritime Services
Board coming to an agreement as to the responsibility
for maintaining the wharf. It was pointed out that
the Trustees are strongly of the opinion that the
retention of the Nielsen Park wharf in good repair is
very much in the public interest, and that the lack of
repairs to the wharf is likely to result in such
deterioration of the entire structure that the safety
of the public will be endangered. Moreover, the
Trustees consider that the Service should call for
expert advice as to the present condition of the
wharf as a matter of urgency. The question of public
risk in regard to persons receiving an injury whilst
on the wharf was raised and Mr.Miller offered to
communicate with the Transport and General Insurance
in regard to this matter.

asset: four chairs and one wall mirror
summary: Mr. Yelland reported that four chairs and one wall mirror from Madame Florence Austral's estate might be loaned to Vaucluse House for the upper corridor, and that the furniture had arrived and was stored in Gilberthorpe's Room for inspection.
quote:
Mr.Yelland reported that, at the last meeting of the
Opera House Trust of which he is a member, the
question arose of the disposal of four chairs and one
wall mirror bequeathed some years ago from the estate
of the late Madame Florence Austral. As the Trustees
of the Opera House Trust had no area in which these
could be displayed, Mr.Yelland suggested that,subject
to the approval of the Trustees of Vaucluse House,the
chairs and mirror might be loaned to Vaucluse House,
thereby contributing to the furnishing of upper
corridor. He had contacted the President who
considered the furniture, being of the right period,
would be most suitable.for this corridor. The
furniture had arrived during the week and was stored
in Gilberthorpe's Room for the Trustees' inspection.

summary: The meeting agreed to order 10,000 Histories of Vaucluse House from the Government Printer at approximately $1,400.00 and pay from the Special Purchase Account.
quote:
The Secretary requested permission to order from the
Government Printer 10,000 Histories of Vaucluse House.
These would cost approximately $1,400-00. It was
agreed to order the Histories, to pay for them from
the Special Purchase Account in the same way as the
folders and postcards are credited.

summary: After Mrs. Newell resigned, the meeting resolved to seek National Parks Service advice on whether the unallocated $9.00 weekly increment should be paid to Mrs. Newell and Mrs. Bickell.
red_flag_reason: A $9.00 weekly increment for two employees was not allocated in the 71/72 budget, so payment was pending advice from the National Parks Service.
quote:
The Secretary reported that one of Trust's clerical
staff, Mrs.I.Newell, had resigned on 9th.February and
payment of long-service leave was being held in
abeyance, pending decision by the Trust as to whether
the increment of $9-00 per week as from 16th.August
1971 was to be paid both to Mrs.Newell and Mrs.Bickell.
It was resolved that a letter be sent to the National
Parks Service informing them that, though the Trust
considered this amount of $9-00 increase should be paid
to these two employees, as it was not allocated in the
71/72 budget, the Trust requested the Service's advice.

summary: Because of the Commemoration Service on 19 March, the next Trust meeting was resolved to be held on Sunday, 12 March.
quote:
Because of the Commemoration Service being held on
19th.March, it was resolved to hold the next Trust
meeting on Sunday,12th.March.
